before.rappel_count_note: No source publishes a rappel total for this route, and the count moves with where you start, so no per-station distances are listed. The rope requirement is published and it is not a preference: the top station is a bolted anchor roughly 20-30 ft above the old pitch-6 slung-block anchor, and from it two 70m ropes reach the bolted anchor atop pitch 5 while doubled 60m ropes do not. A 70m lead rope plus a 70m tagline is the stated ideal because it keeps the option of rappelling from the very top; a party on 60s has to start lower, from partway through the 4th-class scrambling on pitch 7. Most parties do not rappel this at all — they top out on the East Shoulder and take the walk-off, a very exposed and sketchy 4th-class traverse west into the descent gully, which most keep the rope on for despite poor protection.

rappel_detail.pull: On two 70s this is close to a full-length rappel, so set the knot well clear of the lip and knot the ends.
rappel_detail.notes: Top anchor allowing a rappel from the very top of the route with double 70m ropes.
rappel_detail.anchor: Bolted station ~20-30 ft above the old P6 slung-block anchor
hazards: Rope choice is decided at this station and the margin is not discretionary: from the top anchor two 70 m ropes reach the bolted anchor atop pitch 5, and doubled 60 m ropes DO NOT reach between them
The older slung-block anchor below the bolts is still the more obvious thing to see; it is not the current station
rappel_detail.station: The top station is a BOLTED anchor sitting roughly 20-30 ft above the old slung-block anchor at the top of pitch 6 - the old block is the landmark, the bolts are above it. Parties who do not want the full-length first rappel start instead from partway through the 4th-class scrambling on pitch 7.

rappel_detail.notes: Described generically as an 'obvious, good-quality anchor'.
hazards: Slab above and below with little to stand on, so arrive at the anchor rather than near it - there is nothing to grab if you end up off line
rappel_detail.station: The bolted anchor at the top of pitch 5, immediately above the route's very thin slab crux. This is the station the first rappel is measured to, and the reason two 70 m ropes are the published requirement.

rappel_detail.notes: Same as above; individual rappel lengths aren't known.

before.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb the exposed 'Stegosaur' ridge crest pitch (3rd/low-5th class scrambling along a knobby, horn-studded ridge) back down to the notch just below the summit block — most parties downclimb this rather than rappel it. From that notch, make two single-rope rappels (a 30m or 60m single-strand rope is sufficient for each) down the north face back to the Concord-Lexington col; documented descents used natural gear anchors — slings around horns — rather than fixed bolts or chains, so bring extra webbing/cord to back up or replace tat. Total time from summit to the col is about 20 minutes for a competent party. From the col, reverse the approach: descend the talus/heather gully back to the Blue Lake climbers' path and follow it back to the Blue Lake Trail and trailhead. Many parties link this route with a Concord Tower climb, rappelling from Concord's summit into the shared col before starting Lexington's North Face, so plan rope/anchor needs accordingly if doing a link-up.

days.note: A short, fun 3-pitch 5.7 outing that stays in the shade most of the morning — many parties deliberately start a bit later than a typical alpine start to let the face warm up. Approach up the Blue Lake Trail and climbers' trail to the Concord-Lexington col, then 3 pitches (5.7 crux low, easing to 5.4-5.6) to the notch between the summits.

itinerary.totalNote: A short-to-moderate single day: roughly 6-7 hours car-to-car for a fit party, ~2,300 ft gain over 3 pitches — one of the more approachable towers in the Liberty Bell group.
